A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 31-page versions of SHINE, including Appendices A-E. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction/completion evaluations, QA scores, runtime measurements, scaling experiments, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including SHINE's QA performance, efficiency measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Memory extraction, alternating row/column M2P attention, LoRA generation, training objectives, and the SHINE-R recurrence are unchanged. The architecture details in Appendix A also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining, MQA/1QA, LongBench, and supplementary multitask coverage. LongBench was already evaluated in v2; its newly added citation does not introduce a benchmark or scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including Naive, In-Context, SFT, Generative Adapter, the cited SEAL/PaST results, and the appendix LoRA/DoRA/IA3 comparisons.

E3.justification: Models, splits, metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures are retained. Section 5.5 clarifies the description of training with contexts up to 18K tokens without reporting a revision to a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The data-size and architecture ablations, scaling experiments, SFT budget sweeps, and context-quality/length analyses are unchanged. Appendix E contains the same experiments and findings.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the same mean, median, and 10th/90th-percentile reporting. No seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty reporting practice, or statistical testing procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The result tables and plotted findings match, including all appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains SHINE's 55.6 F1 and 0.3-second amortizable time, and Table 5 retains SHINE-R's 19.87 on QMSum.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, architecture equations, computational and memory derivations, and parameter-count analysis are unchanged, including Equations 1-47 and Appendices A-C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about expressive context-to-LoRA generation, adaptation without test-time optimization, efficiency, QA performance, and scaling potential.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations for multi-turn degradation, SHINE-R's gap to In-Context, and weak GSM8K performance. Architecture interpretations and applicability qualifications in Appendices C and E also match.

D1.justification: Section 5.5 now explicitly associates both continued pretraining and fine-tuning with long contexts up to 18K tokens; v2 attached that limit explicitly to fine-tuning. This is a limited documentation clarification. Hardware, other hyperparameters, data-generation instructions, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bai et al. (2024) as the LongBench citation in Section 5.5 and the bibliography. Research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix C is unchanged; other reference edits concern bibliographic metadata and formatting.

P1.justification: Limited edits rephrase the long-context training sentence, change 'Impact Statements' to 'Impact Statement', and update bibliographic metadata. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds running title headers, adjusts section starts and table placement, and improves bibliography URL wrapping. This fixes overflow visible in v2, including a URL clipped at the page edge on page 16. Figure designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a limited improvement in attribution and readability: it supplies the missing LongBench citation, clarifies the long-context training description, and fixes overflowing bibliography URLs. The methods, experimental evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is modest.
